classification.difficultyReason: The same sequence as the reference: compute statistics, identify the outlier, recompute without it and comment. The final part chooses the better measure of centre, which is a similar judgement.

content.prompt:
The number of customers served at a Fremantle café on each of 7 days was recorded as

$62,\ 58,\ 65,\ 61,\ 64,\ 59,\ 12$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the mean, median and range of this data.

answer.short: Mean: $\frac{381}{7}\approx54.4$ customers; median: $61$ customers; range: $53$ customers.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Mean}&=\frac{62+58+65+61+64+59+12}{7}\\\text{Mean}&=\frac{381}{7}\\\text{Mean}&\approx54.4\text{ customers}\end{align*}$$
Ordered data: $12,\ 58,\ 59,\ 61,\ 62,\ 64,\ 65$. The middle value is $61$, so the median is $61$ customers.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=65-12\\\text{Range}&=53\text{ customers}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Identify the outlier in this set of data.

answer.worked: $12$ customers is the outlier because it is much lower than the other values, which are between $58$ and $65$ customers.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Ignore the outlier and calculate the mean, median and range of the remaining 6 values.

Comment on how the summary statistics have changed.

answer.short:
Mean: $61.5$ customers; median: $61.5$ customers; range: $7$ customers.
The mean increases considerably (by about $7.1$), the median increases by $0.5$, and the range decreases from $53$ to $7$.
answer.worked:
Remaining values in order: $58,\ 59,\ 61,\ 62,\ 64,\ 65$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Mean}&=\frac{58+59+61+62+64+65}{6}\\\text{Mean}&=\frac{369}{6}\\\text{Mean}&=61.5\text{ customers}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{61+62}{2}\\\text{Median}&=61.5\text{ customers}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=65-58\\\text{Range}&=7\text{ customers}\end{align*}$$
The mean increases from about $54.4$ to $61.5$. The median increases from $61$ to $61.5$, a rise of $0.5$. The range decreases from $53$ to $7$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Which is the better measure of centre for the number of customers on a typical day, the mean or the median of the original data? Explain.

answer.short: The median. It is $61$ customers, close to a typical day, while the mean of about $54.4$ is pulled below every other day by the outlier.
answer.worked: With the outlier, the mean is about $54.4$ customers, which is lower than all six other days ($58$ to $65$). The median is $61$ customers, which is close to these days. The outlier distorts the mean but affects the median very little, so the median is the better measure of centre.
